sections.h2: Who records deeds in Wyoming County, PA?
sections.html:
The Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds office at the county seat in Tunkhannock records every deed and mortgage for Wyoming County. One elected office handles both jobs, so estate filings and real estate documents are processed under the same roof.

The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and takes no filings after 3:45 p.m. The main number is (570) 996-2361. Payment is by cash or check only, and the office does not accept e-recording, e-filing or electronic signatures, so a seller's closing agent has to deliver or mail the paper deed with original signatures.

Real estate records here go back to 1842, the year the county was carved out of Luzerne County. Documents recorded before February 2007 are indexed by book and page. Anything recorded after that carries an instrument number. If you are selling a house in Wyoming County, either number lets you pull up the vesting deed on the county's online deed search.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Wyoming County?
sections.html:
The base fee for a deed is $64.75 under the schedule that took effect December 1, 2025. That price covers up to four pages and four names. Each page past four adds $2.00, and each name past four adds $0.50.

Fees for the paperwork that usually travels with a sale are below. The office also announced that its lien search fee would become a $20 flat charge and its map filing fee $30 on November 1, 2026, so ask the office for the current schedule before you mail a check.

Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds base fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025 (source: county fee schedule)
DocumentBase fee
Deed$64.75
Mortgage$64.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$61.75
Release or assignment of mortgage$59.75
Easement$59.75
Affidavit or power of attorney$18.50
Military discharge (DD-214)No charge

Exact payment matters. The office keeps overages of $5.00 or less, returns the document when the overage is larger, and gives no refunds. Make the check payable to the Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: How much is realty transfer tax on a Wyoming County sale?
sections.html:
The county recorder states the total at 2 percent of the sale price: 1 percent to the Commonwealth and 1 percent as the local share for the municipality and school district. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue confirms the state portion is 1 percent and that the recorder collects it with any local tax.

On a $215,400 sale, which matches the Census median home value for the county, the combined bill would be $4,308. The recorder will not accept the deed until the tax is paid, and Wyoming County lets a single check cover one taxable transaction. It does not ask for separate checks for transfer tax.

Some transfers are exempt, including conveyances between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and brothers and sisters. The recorder's own FAQ advises checking with an attorney before relying on an exemption. A transfer that claims an exemption, or that states a value different from the consideration on the deed, needs a Statement of Value form filed in duplicate.

sections.h2: What does the recorder check before accepting a deed?
sections.html:
The office rejects documents that fail formatting or acknowledgment rules, so the deed should be right before it is mailed. Its published requirements include these points:

  • Original signatures with a proper notary acknowledgment, dated no earlier than the deed itself. Photocopies cannot be recorded.
  • Type no smaller than size 9, a half inch of blank margin across the top of every page, no color pages, and no staples.
  • The municipality, county and state of the property written on the document, with the dollar consideration matching the figure in numerals.
  • A signed certification of address on every deed and mortgage.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope large enough for the return of the original.

Wyoming County does not require a parcel or PIN number to record a deed. Two situations call for extra paper: land that sits in more than one municipality needs a Statement of Value showing the whole-number percentage split for local transfer tax, and any taxable sale in Windham Township needs one to confirm the school district.

A corrective or confirmatory deed must include a Statement of Value, an explanation of the correction, and a copy of the earlier deed. The office says it does not verify what a document says. It only checks that the requirements are met and the money is paid.

sections.h2: How long does recording take and how do I get a copy?
sections.html:
Expect the recorded original back in about a week, depending on workload, because each document is proofed, scanned, indexed and verified before it is mailed to you. The staff cannot add, delete or change a name on a recorded deed. A new deed is needed for that.

Anyone can search the records free at the courthouse computers or through the online deed search on the county website. Copies of recorded documents can be had in person or online, and certified copies cost $5.00 for up to eight pages, then $0.50 for each page after that. The office searches by full name only. For ownership by parcel number or street address, use the county GIS website or call the assessment office.

Mortgage liens work differently. The recorder holds mortgages and UCC filings, while other liens and judgments are kept at the Prothonotary, Clerk of Courts or Orphans' Court. A seller with unpaid judgments should look there as well as at the recorder.

sections.h2: What is Wyoming County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Wyoming County is a rural county of about 397 square miles of land in Northeast Pennsylvania, with 25,790 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, down 1.1 percent from the 2020 count. Its municipalities are the boroughs of Tunkhannock, Factoryville, Nicholson, Meshoppen and Laceyville, plus townships around them. About 95 percent of residents live in rural areas.

The North Branch of the Susquehanna River crosses the county, and the surface is hilly, with Mehoopany, Tunkhannock, Knob and Bowman's mountains taking up part of it. US 6, US 11 and PA 29 are among the main routes. Winters are cold: average monthly temperatures in Tunkhannock run from about 25 degrees in January to about 71 in July, which matters for roofs, pipes and heating costs when a buyer's inspector walks the house.

  • Housing units: 12,989 in 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.9 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $215,400.
  • Median gross rent: $943.
  • Median household income: $72,460, and 24.3 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Those figures come from Census QuickFacts. A heavily owner-occupied, older population often means inherited houses and estate sales, and the Register of Wills side of the same office is where letters and inheritance tax forms are filed for those cases.

faqs.q: Does Wyoming County accept e-recording for deeds?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder of Deeds states that it does not accept e-recording, e-filing or e-signatures. Deliver the paper deed in person or by mail, with original notary signatures and a self-addressed stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: What is the realty transfer tax rate in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent of the price, split 1 percent state and 1 percent local, according to the county's fee schedule and FAQ. The deed is not accepted until the tax is paid, and the office takes one check for one taxable transaction.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel number to record my deed in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: No. The recorder says it does not require or certify PIN numbers. It does require the municipality, county and state on the document, and a Statement of Value when land lies in several municipalities or in Windham Township.

faqs.q: How much does the Wyoming County recorder charge for a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: A satisfaction piece is $61.75 on the schedule effective December 1, 2025, which covers four pages and four names. A mortgage release or assignment is $59.75. Lenders usually file the satisfaction, and the recorder cannot do it for you.

faqs.q: Where do I find who owns a property in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: Use the county GIS website or call the assessment office, which can look up ownership by parcel number or address. The recorder can only search by full name, and the online deed search shows recorded documents back to 1842.
